findings: Dispatch gate is sound: patient dispatch is reachable only after an acquisition poll returns status COMPLETE with remote.status VALIDATED; missing remote key, unknown, or failed states fail closed to ACQUISITION_STOPPED, and a non-COMPLETE poll worker stops as ACQUISITION_WORKER_BLOCKED, all before any mutation.

Immediate gate recheck: dispatch() re-runs approval() directly before the single patient mutation, re-verifying the review record (returncode, subtype, verdict, scope, reviewed_commit, response SHA-256, claude-fable-5 in assistant_message_models), re-hashing both bound source files, and re-invoking acquisition.reviewed() and patient.require_patient_review(); any failure raises before the mutation.

Single mutation with no retries: exactly one patient.worker execution call per run; any result other than COMPLETE plus DISPATCHED_NOT_YET_VALIDATED returns DISPATCH_BLOCKED without retry; all other adapter calls are read-only polls.
Serial worker sessions: adapter calls are strictly sequential with no concurrency, each in a fresh attempt-N subdirectory of the exclusive private destination.

Bounded observation: both loops cap at 60 polls with fixed 5-minute pauses (~5 hours per phase), covering the unchanged 4-hour acquisition and 60-minute patient analysis limits without extending or purchasing compute; limit exhaustion and every failure branch terminate with a fixed status string.
Operator transfer boundary respected: patient VALIDATED terminates with NEEDS_PRIVATE_RETURN_TRANSFER; the controller does not automate the private return.

Fixed archive path: the input path /content/isles-p001-input-16813698/train.7z is a hard-coded literal passed to the approved patient.execution_packet; polling composes only adapter-defined cells (patient.CPU_CELL, patient.poll_cell()).
Output containment: per-event records, latest.json, and outcome.json go through the approved adapter's private_dir/write_private; the only stdout emission is the fixed status enum as JSON.

Synthetic tests cover the core invariants: dispatch-once only after VALIDATED, no dispatch on FAILED/NOT_VISIBLE/unknown acquisition states, and no retry after dispatch failure; no network or patient data involved.

Minor, non-blocking: latest.json is rewritten on every record and assumes write_private permits overwrite within the exclusive directory; observation-limit and worker-blocked branches lack test coverage; a deliberate rerun with a different --private-dir could dispatch a second patient job, so cross-run deduplication rests on the exclusive-destination convention, operator discipline, and adapter-side gating.
